body:
African Collaborations Group (ACG)

Industrialising Sport in Africa through Bankable Infrastructure Ecosystems

Contact Us ↗
  • A strategic project origination and collaboration platform
  • Convening government, private sector, development finance institutions, sport bodies and academia
  • Carrying projects from concept to operations as accountable strategic lead

Why this matters

Africa’s sport potential is massive, but the existing infrastructure model has lagged behind.

Stadiums are built for matchdays.  A typical stadium hosts 25 to 30 event days a year. For the other 335 to 340 days the lights are off and the maintenance bills still arrive.

Across Africa, major public sporting assets sit idle for most of the year, while the communities around them wait for the jobs and opportunity the investment was meant to create.

A different model exists. It has not yet been applied at scale across the

African continent.

The challenge we are solving

The stadium-only approach has not worked. A new model is needed:

  • Under-utilisation risk (events are episodic; costs are permanent)
  • Operations and maintenance are often under-planned
  • Weak demand assumptions and fragmented stakeholder responsibilities
  • Outcomes: “white elephants”, reputational risk, fiscal burden
  • The consequence: capital spent once, and talent developed abroad. Victory District™ keeps both on African soil.

The familiar failure

01

Designed to an event specification, not to an operating model

02

No anchor tenant and minimal non-event-day utilisation

03

Lifecycle and maintenance costs not provided for in the capital plan

04

Imported design, with limited local supply chain or skills transfer

Our mission

Industrialisation of Sport means turning sport into a repeatable economic model.

From one-off builds to repeatable, investable models

From prestige assets to sustainable operating ecosystems

From isolated venues to integrated sport and entertainment districts

From ad-hoc partnerships to institutional, bankable delivery frameworks

ACG exists to make sport infrastructure investable at scale.

What stands behind ACG

Provenance and backing

Victory District™
What we do

PROVENANCE

Originated inside the FIFA Task Force for Infrastructure Development in Africa.

ACG’s model originated in the FIFA Task Force for Infrastructure Development in Africa, established to advance FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s vision of a FIFA – standard stadium in every African country. APO Group founder Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard was appointed to the Task Force in 2022 by the FIFA Secretary General Fatma Samoura. Within that mandate he led the formation of multi-stakeholder consortium from which the Victory District™ model emerged, carried forward today as an independent initiative.

Explore Victory District™ →

DELIVERY CONSORTIUM

Assembled across every discipline the work demands.

ACG convenes a delivery consortium spanning strategy, masterplanning, feasibility, finance advisory, venue operations, ESG and safeguards.

BACKING AND REACH

APO Group’s networks, credibility and pan-African reach stand directly behind ACG.

The leading, award-winning pan-African communications consultancy and press release distribution service, founded in 2007, trusted by over 300 institutional and blue-chip clients including FIFA, the NBA, Basketball Africa League (BAL), Rugby Africa, the NFL, PFL Africa (MMA) and the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

METHOD

Co-created, never templated.

Every district is evidence-based and shaped by local priorities and market realities.

See what we do →

What ACG is

ACG is a strategic project origination and collaboration platform. It acts as project sponsor and accountable strategic lead, carrying each project from concept to operations with no hand-off.

  1. Concept
  2. Feasibility
  3. Bankability
  4. Delivery
  5. Operations

The stakeholders change at every gate. ACG remains accountable across all five.

ACG originates, structures and leads development by:

  • Creating alignment between stakeholders who rarely work together effectively (government and PPP authorities/regulators, development finance institutions (DFIs), private investors, developers, designers and engineers, legal/transaction and commercial advisors, operators, sport federations/leagues/clubs, event promoters, media/broadcast partners, academia/research, and host communities)
  • Carrying each project through five gates: Concept, Feasibility, Bankability, Delivery and Operations, releasing the next commitment only against the evidence delivered at the last
  • Establishing governance, process discipline, and impact measurement
  • Protecting project integrity through structured stakeholder participation
See what we do →Learn more about our team →

What ACG is not

ACG is not a contractor, and not a substitute for developers, operators or EPC firms.

ACG is a platform: it convenes and leads the full coalition and carries the project end to end, so that the vision and the bankability both hold. Delivery is structured through a dedicated SPV, convening delivery, operating and financing partners under a single structure.

title: Victory District™: from venue to ecosystem
description: Victory District™: from venue to ecosystem
body:
Victory District™: from venue to ecosystem

Victory District™ transforms greenfield and brownfield sites, sports precincts, event venues and underutilised public assets into self-sustaining economic ecosystems. Each district is multi-use, with diversified revenue streams and activity across 365 days rather than matchdays alone.

An established model in mature markets, new to the African continent.

Districts are built to the standards of global sport’s governing bodies, so host nations are eligible to bid for and host international events.

Operations, maintenance and revenue are planned before construction begins, not after handover.

A stadium is a cost. A district is an economy.

Governments end up paying to keep empty stadiums standing. Investors will not back a single income line. The people next to the site want work that does not stop when the builders leave.

Victory District™ is a sport and entertainment district. Five things it has to do, on every site:

  • Fill the calendar: Conferences, concerts, markets and community use, not only the fixture list
  • Earn on ordinary days: Hospitality, retail, leisure and tenants who pay rent all year
  • Keep paying wages once the builders leave: Operations, security, maintenance, hospitality
  • Keep talent at home: Training and academy facilities on the site itself
  • Cover its own running costs: No recurring call on the public purse

The first district proves it. The pipeline is built by repeating it.

ACG is building a pipeline and new category to do that. Flagship project, then blueprint, then replication across Africa. Every project moves through the same gates: Concept, Feasibility, Bankability, Delivery, Operations.

Each one makes the next one faster to fund and easier to approve.

A scalable pipeline, not a single project. ACG is a long-term infrastructure origination engine.

No two districts are the same

Victory District™ is not a fixed master plan template. It is a co-creation framework: the model, mix of uses, governance and commercial structure are shaped through feasibility work with stakeholders. 

The method is the same everywhere.  The answer never is.

The Victory District™ Model

Victory District™ is built on three mutually reinforcing verticals, that have been embedded in the model from the outset. Together these verticals form the Victory District™ Model: providing the framework through which governments, DFIs and investors can assess its viability, impact and scalability.

1. Development

Integrated, mixed-use destinations, anchored by sports facilities and supported by a broad and diversified range of commercial and operational income streams.

2. Events and activation

Attracting major sporting competitions, international events, conferences, entertainment and a wide range of sectoral programmes to the districts.

3. Long-term operations

Professional, sustainable and commercially viable management of the districts, their venues and their supporting infrastructure.

Within these three verticals, every district is designed to:

  • Drive year-round utilisation
  • Expand revenue diversification beyond matchdays
  • Create jobs and youth opportunities
  • Support talent development pathways
  • Enable sustainable operations and maintenance

ACG is building a continental campaign to promote sport as a catalyst for economic development, investment and social impact.

Who benefits and why (stakeholder value)

A platform designed for alignment

Government

Private sector

Investable opportunities, a visible pipeline, and early participation in a new asset class for the continent

Our Team

ACG’s leadership, 28 Advisory Board members, and 12 internationally recognised scholars behind Africa’s most ambitious sport infrastructure origination platform.

Founder and Executive Chairman

Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard

Founder and Executive Chairman, African Collaborations Group (ACG)

Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard is a Franco-Gabonese entrepreneur and the founder of APO Group and African Collaborations Group (ACG). He has been recognised among the 100 Most Influential Africans in 2023 and again in 2024, and has been featured in international media including CNN, Forbes, Forbes Africa, and CNBC Africa.

In 2022, Nicolas was appointed as a member of the FIFA Task Force for Infrastructure Development in Africa, created to support FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s vision of accelerating FIFA-standard sport infrastructure development across the continent. Through that process, he was personally mandated by President Infantino to develop an integrated sport and entertainment district concept for Africa. Building on that experience, he founded African Collaborations Group (ACG) to focus on originating bankable sport and entertainment district projects, moving beyond single-venue development models towards mixed-use, revenue-generating and financially sustainable district ecosystems.

Nicolas holds advisory and governance roles across the wider sport, business, and Africa investment ecosystem. He serves as a Senior Advisory Board Member of the Canada-Africa Chamber of Business, Strategic Advisor to the Chief Executive Officer of the Royal African Society of the United Kingdom (RAS), and Strategic Advisor to the European Union–Africa Chamber of Commerce (EUACC). He is also a Member of the Africa Tech Festival/AfricaCom Leadership Council.

He sits on the Advisory Boards of the African Energy Chamber (AEC), the Critical Minerals Africa Group (CMAG), the World Football Summit (WFS), the Future Hospitality Summit (FHS) (formerly the Africa Hotel Investment Forum, AHIF), and the Africa Women Innovation & Entrepreneurship Forum (AWIEF).

He is a Member of the Pan-African Ubuntu Circle of The ONE Campaign, and an International Committee Member of the All Africa Music Awards (AFRIMA). He also serves as Special Advisor to the President of Rugby Africa, the governing body of rugby in Africa.

Previously, Nicolas was an Advisory Board Member of the EurAfrican Forum (2019–2025), a Member of the Sports Africa Investment Summit (SAIS) Advisory Committee (2024–2025), and an Advisory Board Member of the Bloomberg New Economy Gateway Africa conference (2023). He also served as a semi-final judge of Africa’s Business Heroes (also known as the Jack Ma Prize for Africa) in 2020 and 2021.

More information at www.Pompigne-Mognard.com.

Founding Chief Executive Officer

Paulo J. Cruz

Founding Chief Executive Officer, African Collaborations Group (ACG)

Paulo J. Cruz is the Founding Chief Executive Officer of African Collaborations Group (ACG), where he leads the development of a pan-African platform for structuring institutional-grade sport and entertainment district ecosystems.

Mr Cruz joins ACG from DAMAC Group, one of the largest privately held real estate developers in the Middle East (close to USD 10 billion in property sales in 2025), where he served as Senior Vice President from 2022 to 2026. He brings over 28 years of senior executive experience across real estate, infrastructure and large-scale development in Africa, the Middle East and Europe, having originated and structured projects ranging from USD 50 million to over USD 5 billion.

His expertise lies in transforming early-stage concepts into financially structured, investable developments.

Prior to DAMAC Group, he held senior leadership roles at BlackIvy Group, BP, Movares and Cushman & Wakefield, and previously served as Group Chief Executive Officer of LandAfrique.

At ACG, he leads the execution of the Victory District™ framework, driving investment and sustainable growth while advancing integrated district ecosystems across Africa.

Read more information here.

Our Advisory Board

ACG is supported by an Advisory Board of senior, highly experienced leaders who bring independent perspective, credibility, and real-world execution insight to the development of Victory District™ and future projects.

The Advisory Board exists to strengthen decision-making at the earliest stages of project origination – helping ACG stress-test assumptions, accelerate stakeholder alignment, and ensure the concept evolves into a model that is technically credible, commercially viable, and institutionally deliverable.

Advisory Board members serve in a non-executive, strategic advisory capacity.

They do not manage day-to-day operations; instead, they provide guidance, introductions, and constructive challenge across the core dimensions that make or break complex infrastructure programmes, including governance, bankability, sport ecosystem fit, and long-term operational sustainability.

Our Research and Impact Advisory Panel

To complement its Advisory Board, African Collaborations Group (ACG) has assembled a Research & Impact Advisory Panel of internationally recognised scholars from leading universities around the world, covering sport economics, stadium financing, urban planning, sport architecture, mega-event legacy, environmental sustainability, sport-for-development, and impact assessment. The panel includes two UNESCO Chair holders, the Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of Sports Economics, and scholars who have advised the United Nations, the International Olympic Committee, and the United States Congress.

 

The Panel provides independent academic rigour throughout the pre-feasibility and feasibility phases: stress-testing assumptions, challenging methodology, and validating outcomes before they reach investors and government decision-makers.

 

The Panel advises on the impact narrative across jobs, skills, inclusion, youth pathways and public value; defines practical KPIs, baselines and an evidence plan for feasibility work; stress-tests demand, utilisation and economic impact assumptions; reviews masterplan and architectural coherence; embeds ESG, climate resilience and safeguards thinking early, in a way that withstands due diligence; and peer-reviews key feasibility outputs before they are shared with decision-makers.

 

No other sport infrastructure originator in Africa has assembled a comparable independent academic capability. The Panel exists only within ACG.

description: Former DAMAC Senior Vice President Paulo J. Cruz Appointed Founding CEO of African Collaborations Group (ACG) to Spearhead Sports and Entertainment District Development Across Africa
body:

Former DAMAC Senior Vice President Paulo J. Cruz Appointed Founding CEO of African Collaborations Group (ACG) to Spearhead Sports and Entertainment District Development Across Africa

African Collaborations Group (ACG) (www.ACGafrica.com), the leading strategic project origination and collaboration platform focused on the industrialisation of sport in Africa through bankable district ecosystems, today announced the appointment of Paulo J. Cruz as its Founding Chief Executive Officer.

Mr Cruz joins ACG from DAMAC Group, one of the largest privately held real estate developers in the Middle East, where he served as Senior Vice President from 2022 to 2026. In 2025, the Group reported close to USD 10 billion in property sales. His tenure at DAMAC further deepened an already distinguished career spanning infrastructure origination, urbanisation strategy, and large-scale real estate development across Africa, the Middle East, and Europe.

Over the course of his 28-year career, Mr Cruz has originated or structured projects ranging from USD 50 million to in excess of USD 5 billion, stewarding initiatives from early-stage concept through feasibility analysis, financial structuring, and investor alignment to bankable delivery stages. His professional footprint encompasses senior roles at BP, one of the world’s foremost energy companies; BlackIvy Group, a US-backed infrastructure investment platform; Movares, a leading European engineering consultancy; and Cushman & Wakefield, a globally recognised real estate advisory firm.

Prior to DAMAC, Mr Cruz served as Group Chief Executive Officer of LandAfrique, a pan-African development platform focused on industrial parks, infrastructure, housing and power projects across Sub-Saharan Africa, further solidifying his reputation as one of the continent’s most experienced development executives.

As Founding CEO of ACG, Mr Cruz will lead the development and expansion of a pan-African origination platform, working in close partnership with sovereign governments, development finance institutions (DFIs), private investors, sport and entertainment principals, and leading academic institutions to structure district-level projects that are both investable and deliverable at scale.

ACG operates as a specialised origination and collaboration platform engineered to transform concepts into credible, bankable sport and entertainment district ecosystems — architectures capable of attracting institutional capital and generating long-term, multi-dimensional economic impact at a national and continental scale.

ACG’s flagship initiative, Victory District™, provides a proprietary district development framework designed to originate integrated, mixed-use sport and entertainment destinations that transcend conventional single-venue models. The framework prioritises asset utilisation optimisation, long-term sustainability, expanded revenue diversification beyond matchday economics, structured employment and youth opportunity creation, talent development pathways, and institutional-grade operations and maintenance standards.

Sport governing bodies need venues that meet international standards. Broadcasters, sponsors and event organisers need facilities capable of generating commercial value. Every revenue stream in the sport economy ultimately depends on infrastructure existing and its respective operation. ACG CEO Paulo J. Cruz to Speak at the Angola Access & Investment Conference 2026 in Luanda on How Sport and Entertainment Districts Can Drive Inclusive Economic Growth Across Africa

African Collaborations Group (ACG) (www.ACGafrica.com), the leading strategic project origination and collaboration platform focused on the industrialisation of sport in Africa through the origination of bankable sport and entertainment district ecosystems, today announced that its CEO, Paulo J. Cruz, will speak at the Angola Access & Investment Conference 2026 (AAIC) (www.aaic.ao) in Luanda, Angola, from 14 to 17 October 2026.

The AAIC is organised by Expo Connect Angola in partnership with Skyliam Properties, the Cópia Group, and Angolan Business Beyond Borders, with the support of the Angola-Mozambique Chamber of Commerce and Industry (CCIAM) and the Angolan Ministry of Tourism and the Ministry of Telecommunications, Information Technologies, and Social Communication. The conference brings together heads of state, ministers, ambassadors, CEOs, investors, development banks, and business leaders from over 60 international markets.

Mr Cruz will address how ACG’s origination of integrated sport and entertainment districts contributes directly to inclusive economic growth. His intervention will focus on how sport infrastructure, when designed as a financially self-sustaining urban ecosystem, becomes a catalyst for large-scale job creation, skills development, accessible infrastructure, and long-term economic diversification.

The AAIC’s focus on accessibility and inclusion aligns directly with ACG’s approach to sport and entertainment district development. A Victory District™ is designed from inception to serve the widest possible community: creating permanent employment across dozens of professions, providing professional sport training facilities for young athletes, and generating economic activity that benefits surrounding neighbourhoods year-round.

“Sport infrastructure has the power to be one of the most inclusive economic assets a country can build,” said Paulo J. Cruz, CEO of ACG. “A Victory District™ does not just create stadiums. It creates thousands of permanent jobs, from hospitality to broadcast production, from sport coaching to facility management. It creates training pathways for young athletes. And it creates an urban ecosystem that generates economic activity 365 days a year. That is inclusive growth in practice, not in theory. I am honoured to share that vision at the AAIC alongside some of Africa’s most influential investors and decision-makers.”

The AAIC programme includes official MoU signing ceremonies, B2B investment rounds, VIP executive networking with senior government and business leaders across 10 dedicated Business Lounges, and the inauguration of Angola’s first assistive technology factory. The conference covers priority sectors including energy, mining, accessible tourism, agriculture, logistics, health, and infrastructure.

ACG’s Victory District™ framework is designed to originate integrated, mixed-use sport and entertainment districts that move beyond single-venue development models. Each district combines stadiums, indoor arenas, training academies, hotels, conference centres, retail, entertainment, residential, and commercial space within a single masterplanned development, financed by private and institutional capital without reliance on public subsidy.

Mr Cruz brings more than 28 years of experience across Africa, the Middle East, and Europe in originating, structuring, and delivering large-scale infrastructure, urbanisation, and real estate development initiatives. Prior to ACG, he served as Senior Vice President at DAMAC Group, the largest private real estate developer in the Middle East, and as Group CEO of LandAfrique, a pan-African development platform focused on industrial parks, infrastructure, housing, and power projects across Sub-Saharan Africa.

Santiago Bernabéu Stadium Renovation Advisor Carlos Carrión Joins African Collaborations Group (ACG) Advisory Board to Advance Sport and Entertainment Districts Across Africa

African Collaborations Group (ACG) (www.ACGafrica.com), the leading strategic project origination and collaboration platform focused on the industrialisation of sport in Africa through the origination of bankable sport and entertainment district ecosystems, today announced the appointment of Carlos Carrión to its Advisory Board.

Mr Carrión is Partner and Director of Sports & Entertainment at Senn Ferrero, one of the world’s leading advisory firms in sports and entertainment. He also serves as External Advisor to a top-tier European football club, a role he has held since 2018, and brings more than 30 years of professional experience across four continents in the design, business modelling, financing, operation and commercialisation of sport and entertainment venues, having worked at senior level in both multinational corporations and international advisory.

Mr Carrión played a central advisory role in the €600 million redevelopment of the Santiago Bernabéu Stadium, one of the most ambitious stadium transformations of the modern era. The Bernabéu redevelopment redefined what a 21st-century venue can be: an integrated, mixed-use, digitally-enabled facility engineered to generate revenue both on match and non-match days, and designed around mobility, transport, payment and socio-economic data streams that shaped its facility design, operating model and long-term commercial performance. Mr Carrión’s work on the project drew on a career-long study of over 300 venues worldwide, and hands-on advisory work with more than a dozen of them across three continents.

His broader career combines senior positions as head of marketing and sponsorships for globally recognised brands in telecommunications and banking, participation in the international development team of one of Europe’s most prominent football clubs, and consulting engagements across football, Formula 1, MotoGP, Formula E, basketball and other major sport properties. He holds a degree from IE (Instituto de Empresa) and brings a strong marketing, corporate communications, finance and business development background to his advisory work.

His appointment to the ACG Advisory Board brings to the platform the world’s most current and directly relevant expertise on the design, financing and business modelling of large-scale, mixed-use sport and entertainment venues — the very ecosystem logic that ACG is applying at district scale across the African continent. Where the Santiago Bernabéu has become the reference for what a modern, data-driven, revenue-diversified urban sport venue can be, ACG is originating the equivalent thinking at district scale for African markets: not single venues, but integrated, mixed-use, financially sustainable ecosystems that generate value across match, non-match, entertainment, hospitality, retail and community uses.

His appointment brings to the ACG Advisory Board an exceptional combination of venue design and operational expertise, deep experience across four continents and multiple sport properties, hands-on advisory to some of the most valuable sport organisations in the world, and a proven track record on one of the most significant venue redevelopment projects of the past decade — capabilities directly relevant to originating and structuring large-scale sport and entertainment district projects across the African continent.

“Carlos Carrión brings to our Advisory Board a genuinely rare capability: the current, hands-on expertise of building the world’s most advanced sport venue ecosystem. The Santiago Bernabéu redevelopment is the reference project for what a 21st-century venue and its business model can be, and the doctrine that shaped it — mixed use, data-driven, revenue-diversified, designed for match and non-match days alike — is exactly the doctrine ACG is applying at district scale across the African continent. His presence on our Advisory Board significantly strengthens ACG’s technical, commercial and design capabilities as we originate bankable district ecosystems in African markets,” said Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard (www.Pompigne-Mognard.com), Founder and Executive Chairman of ACG.

The ACG Advisory Board provides strategic guidance as ACG originates and structures large-scale sport and entertainment district projects across the continent, aligning governments, development finance institutions (DFIs), investors, sport bodies and infrastructure partners to support the development of financially sustainable, mixed-use district ecosystems.

Africa’s sport economy is projected to reach $20 billion by 2035, yet the continent continues to lack the integrated district ecosystems required to support large-scale development. ACG addresses this gap by originating bankable sport and entertainment district projects, moving beyond single-venue development models towards mixed-use, revenue-generating and financially sustainable district ecosystems.

Through its collaborative model, ACG convenes governments, PPP authorities and regulators, development finance institutions, private investors, developers, designers and engineers, legal and transaction advisors, operators, sport federations and leagues, event promoters, media and broadcast partners, academic institutions and host communities, creating structured pathways from concept to feasibility, bankability and delivery.

Paulo Gomes, Former World Bank Executive Director for Africa and AfroChampions Co-Chair Joins African Collaborations Group (ACG) Advisory Board to Advance Sport and Entertainment Districts Across Africa

African Collaborations Group (ACG) (www.ACGafrica.com), a strategic project origination and collaboration platform focused on the industrialisation of sport in Africa through the origination of bankable sport and entertainment district ecosystems, today announced the appointment of Paulo Gomes to its Advisory Board.

Mr Gomes is Founder, Chairman, & CEO of Constelor Investment Holdings, a pan-African investment management and strategic advisory firm, and Founder and Chairman of Orango Investment Corporation, a strategic advisory and investment platform dedicated to advancing Africa’s investment agenda under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). He is also Co-Chair of the AfroChampions Initiative, the flagship pan-African platform promoting the economic and industrial transformation of the continent.

He brings to the ACG Advisory Board more than 30 years of executive experience in sovereign advisory, infrastructure finance and corporate investment across Africa. From 1998 to 2006, Mr Gomes served on the Board of the World Bank Group, first as Alternate Executive Director and then as Executive Director from 2002 to 2006, representing 25 African countries and playing an instrumental role in the launch of the Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) and in securing more than USD 1 billion for the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s post-conflict recovery.

A founding member of both the Africa Finance Corporation and the Green Climate Fund — the world’s largest dedicated fund supporting developing countries in climate mitigation and adaptation — Mr Gomes has been at the heart of the creation of several of the institutions that shape modern African finance. Through Orango, he has advised several African sovereign funds (including Angola and Senegal), and participated in the resource mobilization strategy of the ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development, and currently serves as strategy advisor to a leading African industrial group on its continental expansion.

Mr Gomes is a co-founder of Geronimo, an integrated cocoa value chain initiative developed with Chocolaterie de Monaco and Afreximbank, and of Alta Mar, a sustainable aquaculture venture. He chairs the Advisory Board of the Africa–South East Asia Chamber of Commerce (ASEACC) based in Singapore, and has been appointed Distinguished Visiting Fellow at the NTU-SBF Centre for African Studies, a fellowship funded by the Government of Singapore, positioning him at the interface between African and Asian capital and trade.

His board memberships have included Ecobank Transnational Inc., ASKY Airlines, AFIG Private Equity Fund, the African Capacity Building Foundation, the African Media Initiative, Roll Back Malaria, NSIA Ivory Coast and Alta Mar Norway. He also chairs the BioGuinée Foundation in Guinea-Bissau.

Mr Gomes holds a Master’s in Public Administration (MPA) in Economic Policy and Management from Harvard University’s John F. Kennedy School of Government and a Bachelor’s degree in Economics and International Trade from Sciences Po and the Institut Libre d’Étude des Relations Internationales (ILERI), Paris.

Extending the AfroChampions logic into this domain is precisely why I am joining the ACG Advisory Board,” said Paulo Gomes.

description: Sport Infrastructure in Africa: BBC World News Interviews ACG Founder Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard on the Transformation Ahead
body:

Sport Infrastructure in Africa: BBC World News Interviews ACG Founder Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard on the Transformation Ahead

In an interview with BBC World News, African Collaborations Group (ACG) (www.ACGafrica.com) Founder and Executive Chairman Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard set out the case for transforming Africa’s sport infrastructure — arguing that the continent’s sport economy potential will remain theoretical without the right infrastructure, and that the model needed is not the isolated stadium but the integrated, multi-purpose sport and entertainment district.

The full interview can be listened to here: https://apo-opa.co/4rlutKe

Africa’s population of 1.5 billion is projected to reach 2.5 billion by 2050, and its sport economy is projected to reach $20 billion by 2035. Yet, as Mr Pompigne-Mognard told the BBC, this potential will remain theoretical without the infrastructure to support it. So far, he noted, Africa has produced “white elephants” — stadiums built for a single event, empty the rest of the year and draining public finance.

The capital to close this infrastructure gap already exists, Mr Pompigne-Mognard told the BBC. Development finance institutions have substantial resources allocated for African infrastructure, but that capital is not being deployed at scale because bankable projects are not being brought forward. ACG has been established specifically to close that gap, by originating integrated, multi-purpose, multi-sport district ecosystems that combine stadiums with restaurants, cinemas, conference centres, malls, gyms and schools — alive 365 days a year, generating revenue on both event and non-event days.

The interview also addressed ACG’s Advisory Board rollout, which has attracted senior figures from across global sport including former FIFA Secretary General Fatma Samoura and Carlos Carrión, advisor on the €600 million renovation of Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabéu Stadium. As Mr Pompigne-Mognard explained, each Advisory Board member brings a specific set of skills, and all are aligned on a shared conviction: Africa’s sport economy potential cannot be reached without the right infrastructure.

Full interview transcript

BBC World News

Piers Edwards (BBC):

Finally, is the staging of sports events in Africa set to change? In recent days, a company called the African Collaborations Group has been announcing some notable figures on its advisory board. The group wants to bring together different parties to fundamentally change the way in which the continent hosts sport. Franco-Gabonese Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard is both founder and executive chairman.

Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard:

Africa has 1.5 billion people today, projected to reach 2.5 billion by 2050. Its sports economy is projected to reach 20 billion dollars by 2035. But without sport infrastructure, that potential will remain entirely theoretical.

And so far, Africa has only produced what are referred to as white elephants, stadiums built for one event, empty the rest of the year and draining public finance.

But the capital to fix this actually exists. On one side, you have development financial institutions with billions allocated for African infrastructure that they cannot deploy simply because no one is bringing them bankable projects.

On the other side, you have governments who have the political will. And then you have the sport governing bodies who have the demand. They want to organise competitions across the continent and they are looking for African countries to host those competitions. But for lack of infrastructure, they cannot do that.

And so we think completely differently. The way we have structured our concept is to think about a multi-purpose, multi-sport, not stadium, but district.

So yes, you do have a stadium, but as part of an entire ecosystem including restaurants, cinema, conference centre, mall, gym,…

We are even talking about schools, etc., to make sure that district is alive 365 days a year, never goes dark. And that’s how you build an ecosystem, an entire economy.

Piers Edwards (BBC):

You’ve brought some big names on board. And one of the biggest, of course, is Fatma Samoura, who was the former Secretary General at FIFA. I saw also that you had an individual who was involved in the renovation project for the Santiago Bernabéu stadium, obviously around Madrid’s home ground. That’s quite some expertise to have on board.

Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard:

Well, all the members of the advisory board are on that advisory board for a reason. Each one of them has a specific set of skills.

And each one of them is aligned on the fact that, yes, there is a huge potential for the business of sport, for the economy of sport in Africa.

But for all of them, it is absolutely obvious that without the right infrastructure, we’ll never reach that potential.

On ACG’s model:

“What I find interesting about ACG is that it looks beyond the traditional stadium model, towards sport and entertainment districts that work all year round, combining sport with hospitality, entertainment, retail, training and community facilities.”

“Nigeria could become a regional hub for major competitions, entertainment productions and talent development.”

On Africa’s talent drain:

“Africa’s sporting talent is world class, but the infrastructure to develop, retain and fully benefit from that talent is still largely absent.”

“The real question is how to turn that potential into bankable projects, quality jobs and long-term value for Nigerians.”

African Collaborations Group (ACG) (www.ACGAfrica.com), a strategic project origination and collaboration platform focused on the industrialisation of sport in Africa, is recruiting a Founding Chief Executive Officer.

ACG has recently been granted an Exclusive Mandate by a major African country to originate, structure, coordinate, and advance an innovative sport and entertainment district, from early concept through feasibility and towards bankability.

This is a rare opportunity to lead a first-of-its-kind, continent-scale initiative at the intersection of infrastructure development, urban regeneration, sport, youth employment, and long-term economic impact.

ABOUT AFRICAN COLLABORATIONS GROUP (ACG)

African Collaborations Group (ACG) is a strategic project origination and collaboration platform focused on industrializing sport in Africa through bankable sport and entertainment infrastructure ecosystems. We convene the full stakeholder “table” — including government and PPP authorities, DFIs, private investors, developers, operators, designers, academics, and specialist legal and commercial advisers — to move projects from concept to feasibility and towards bankability with disciplined governance and measurable impact.

ACG’s flagship initiative, Victory District™, is a co-creation framework for sport and entertainment districts designed for year‑round utilisation, diversified revenues, sustainable operations, and strong social and economic outcomes.

ROLE PURPOSE

The Founding CEO will lead ACG’s flagship Victory District™ proof-of-concept from mandate-driven mobilisation and feasibility through to bankability and financial close, while establishing the governance, operating cadence and stakeholder alignment required for successful delivery. A central part of the role is to architect, secure and institutionalise ACG’s commercial model and income architecture for the flagship project—ensuring it is coherent, defensible and fully embedded in the feasibility and transaction pathway (rather than treated as an afterthought). The CEO will build the platform, playbook and credibility needed to scale ACG into a repeatable, continent-wide sport infrastructure origination engine.

ROLE SUMMARY

The Founding CEO will be responsible for:

  • Leading the execution of the first Victory District™ project from feasibility through to bankability and financial close, and ensuring an orderly transition into delivery.
  • Coordinating a high-calibre international consortium of advisers and delivery partners under a disciplined governance and reporting cadence.
  • Managing government and DFI relationships at senior, institutional level, and maintaining trust, momentum and alignment.
  • Architecting and securing ACG’s commercial model and income architecture for the flagship project, ensuring it is contractually documented, bankable, and embedded in the feasibility and transaction pathway.
  • Driving commercial structuring, SPV preparation and multi-stakeholder alignment across public and private stakeholders.
  • Building ACG into Africa’s leading sport infrastructure origination and development platform, with a scalable pipeline and repeatable playbook.

This role is suited to a senior infrastructure executive with strong project origination experience across PPPs, DFIs and/or sovereign development, ready to step into a founding, continent-scale leadership mandate.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Leadership

  • Lead the full development cycle of Victory District™ (concept → feasibility → bankability pathway/PPP → SPV → financial close), and oversee the handover into delivery.
  • Define ACG’s long-term strategy, platform positioning, project pipeline and expansion across African markets.
  • Establish and run a disciplined operating cadence (workplan delivery, steering committee rhythm, reporting, risk and decision logs).

Government & Institutional Engagement

  • Represent ACG with Ministers, Heads of State, DFIs and international organisations.
  • Lead negotiations and alignment on MoUs, PPP/concession frameworks and SPV arrangements with sovereign authorities and relevant regulators.
  • Maintain a credible institutional interface, ensuring stakeholder engagement is orderly, controlled and consistent with confidentiality obligations.

Consortium Management

  • Coordinate global partners, including financial, legal, design and technical advisers, ensuring clear scopes, accountability and delivery standards.
  • Ensure feasibility, PPP and transaction outputs meet DFI and investment-committee expectations (governance, due diligence readiness, auditability and transparency).
  • Manage performance of partners and maintain ACG’s authority within the consortium governance framework.

Commercial & Financial Structuring

  • Design and implement ACG’s revenue architecture for the flagship project, ensuring it is commercially coherent, defensible, and aligned with procurement/PPP realities.
  • Ensure ACG’s commercial entitlements are properly reflected in feasibility assumptions, SPV budgets and transaction documentation, and do not “disappear” during structuring.
  • Oversee investor engagement and readiness for financial close, including coordination of commercial terms, risk allocation and capital formation strategy.
